calls.reason: The UK white paper reports concerns about regulatory fragmentation, and the BLOOM study measures training emissions. Neither shows that common standards avoid country-specific training or its emissions.

EU-wide obligations took effect, and Google documented participation in shaping the code and committed to signing alongside other providers. This supports taking shared rules seriously, though it does not establish completed compliance.

HIIG and GovAI surveys show strong support among selected experts, while YouGov finds public uncertainty. These do not settle the rhetorical claim of near-universal recognition of benefits, risks and urgency.
